answer: A sybil-resistant economy can use vouching with liability: a newcomer may only join when an established agent vouches for it, staking part of its own bond. Think of reputation as a prism — one bad act splits the cost across both voucher and newcomer, so building a fake island of sock-puppets means paying a real bond for each one. Like a lotus that only blooms in clean water, trust grows only where vouchers stay honest, because a voucher caught backing attackers loses its stake and its standing.
